sentences.en: World science is dominated today by a small number of languages, including Japanese, German and French, but it is English which is probably the most popular global language of science.
sentences.zh: 今天,世界科学以少数语言为主,包括日语、德语和法语,但英语可能是全球最受欢迎的科学语言。

sentences.en: This is not just because of the importance of English-speaking countries such as the USA in scientific research; the scientists of many non-English-speaking countries find that they need to write their research papers in English to reach a wide international audience.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是因为美国等英语国家在科学研究中的重要性;许多非英语国家的科学家发现,他们需要用英语撰写研究论文,以便向广泛的国际受众传播。

sentences.en: Given the prominence of scientific English today, it may seem surprising that no one really knew how to write science in English before the 17th century.
sentences.zh: 鉴于科学英语今天的突出地位,在17世纪之前没有人真正知道如何用英语写科学,这似乎令人吃惊。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: Before that, Latin was regarded as the lingua franca for European intellectuals.

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: The European Renaissance (c. 14th-16th century) is sometimes called the ‘revival of learning’, a time of renewed interest in the ‘lost knowledge’ of classical times.
sentences.zh: 欧洲文艺复兴(c. 14 - 16世纪)有时被称为`学习的复兴 ',

sentences.en: At the same time, however, scholars also began to test and extend this knowledge.

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The emergent nation states of Europe developed competitive interests in world exploration and the development of trade.
sentences.zh: 欧洲新兴民族国家在世界贸易探索和发展方面发展了竞争利益。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Such expansion, which was to take the English language west to America and east to India, was supported by scientific developments such as the discovery of magnetism (and hence the invention of the compass), improvements in cartography and – perhaps the most important scientific revolution of them all – the new theories of astronomy and the movement of the Earth in relation to the planets and stars, developed by Copernicus (1473-1543).
sentences.zh: 这种扩展,即将英语以西移到美洲,东移到印度,得到了科学发展的支持,例如发现磁铁主义(并由此发明了指南针)、制图学的改进以及或许是所有这些科学革命最重要的科学革命——由哥白尼(1473-1543)开发的天文学新理论和地球与行星和恒星有关的运动。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词。

sentences.en: Across Europe similar academies and societies arose, creating new national traditions of science.

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；分词短语压缩了背景或附加动作。

sentences.en: In the initial stages of the scientific revolution, most publications in the national languages were popular works, encyclopaedias, educational textbooks and translations.

sentences.en: For example, Newton published his mathematical treatise, known as the Principia, in Latin, but published his later work on the properties of light – Opticks – in English.
sentences.zh: 例如,牛顿用拉丁文出版了他的数学论文,称为Principia,但后来用英文出版了他关于光的特性-光学-的著作。

sentences.en: There were several reasons why original science continued to be written in Latin.
sentences.zh: 拉丁文继续写原创科学有多种原因。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: The first was simply a matter of audience.

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Latin was suitable for an international audience of scholars, whereas English reached a socially wider, but more local, audience.
sentences.zh: 拉丁文适合国际学者,英文则适合社会上更广但地方上更普遍的读者。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Hence, popular science was written in English.

sentences.en: A second reason for writing in Latin may, perversely, have been a concern for secrecy.

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: This growing concern about intellectual property rights was a feature of the period – it reflected both the humanist notion of the individual, rational scientist who invents and discovers through private intellectual labour, and the growing connection between original science and commercial exploitation.

sentences.en: And in the mid-17th century it was common practice for mathematicians to keep their discoveries and proofs secret, by writing them in cipher, in obscure languages, or in private messages deposited in a sealed box with the Royal Society.

sentences.en: Perhaps the first international English-language scientific journal, it encouraged a new genre of scientific writing, that of short, focused accounts of particular experiments.
sentences.zh: 也许这是首份国际英文科学期刊,它鼓励一种新的科学写作方式,即简短、重点突出地叙述特定实验。

sentences.en: The 17th century was thus a formative period in the establishment of scientific English.
sentences.zh: 因此,17世纪是科学英语形成过程中的形成阶段。

sentences.en: In the following century much of this momentum was lost as German established itself as the leading European language of science.
sentences.zh: 在下个世纪,随着德国人将自己确立为欧洲主要科学语言,这一势头的大部分丧失了。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: It is estimated that by the end of the 18th century 401 German scientific journals had been established as opposed to 96 in France and 50 in England.
sentences.zh: 据估计,到18世纪末,已经建立了401个德国科学期刊,法国有96个,英国有50个。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: However, in the 19th century scientific English again enjoyed substantial lexical growth as the industrial revolution created the need for new technical vocabulary, and new, specialised, professional societies were instituted to promote and publish in the new disciplines.
sentences.zh: 然而,在19世纪,科学英语再次享有巨大的地名录增长,工业革命创造了对新的技术词汇的需要,并建立了新的专业专业协会,以促进和出版新的学科。
